mainTopic: Interrupting תפלה for danger, and where rain and הבדלה go in the עמידה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of the חסיד who would not answer an officer during תפלה, using a קל וחומר from standing before a human king. The גמרא then limits the rule about a snake: one does not stop for a snake, but does stop for a scorpion or for approaching oxen. It ends that section with the story of רבי חנינא בן דוסא and the עַרְוָד, teaching that sin, not the creature, is what kills. A new משנה then places the mention of rain, the request for rain, and הבדלה in specific ברכות of the עמידה. רב יוסף and the רבנן explain why each addition fits its ברכה, which leads to a short praise of דעה and the מקדש. The גמרא next explains how הבדלה moved between תפלה and the כוס, and rules that saying it in one does not exempt the other. A ברייתא that seems to say otherwise is corrected to avoid a ברכה שאינה צריכה. Finally, רב ששת rules that one who erred in both places goes back to the beginning.

steps.title: What would happen if the officer answered?
steps.stepSummary: The pious man gets the officer to say that answering someone while standing before a human king could cost him his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you answer him? No. And if you did answer him, what would they do to you? They would cut off my head with a sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The pious man asks the officer about answering someone while standing before a king. This exchange sets up the comparison he will make next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer says he would not answer. He then explains that answering could bring a severe punishment.

phrases.english: Would you answer him?! He said to him: No.
And if you had answered him,
what would they have done to you?
He said to him: They would cut off
my head with a sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a conversation that began on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the officer would answer someone while standing before a king, and what answering would cost him.

steps.title: A human king becomes the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The pious man uses the officer’s answer to explain why he would not interrupt his prayer before הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is this not a matter of reasoning from the lighter case to the stronger one? If you act this way before a human king, who is here today and in the grave tomorrow, then all the more so I, standing before the eternal King of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: The pious man draws a קל וחומר from the officer’s own answer. He explains why he did not respond during prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer would not interrupt an encounter with a mortal king. The pious man argues that standing before הקב״ה is an even stronger reason not to interrupt.

keyTerms.meaning: reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one
the Holy One, blessed be He

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: He said to him: Is this not a matter of reasoning from the lighter case to the stronger one?
If you, who were standing
before a king of flesh and blood,
who is here today and in the grave tomorrow—
[you would act] thus; then I, who was standing
before the King of kings
the Holy One, blessed be He,
who lives and endures forever
and for all eternity—
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר,
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the officer’s answers as the basis for a stronger comparison.
steps.raayaObject: The pious man’s refusal to interrupt his prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The officer’s admission that he would not answer someone while standing before a human king.

steps.title: The officer accepts the explanation
steps.stepSummary: The officer is appeased, and the pious man goes home safely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately that officer was appeased, and that pious man departed for his home in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The story closes. The officer accepts the explanation and lets the pious man leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר answers the officer’s complaint within the story. No new rule is introduced in this closing line.

phrases.english: Immediately that officer was appeased,
and that pious man departed for his home in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the result of the pious man’s explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The officer accepts the pious man’s reason for not responding.

steps.title: The rule about a snake during prayer
steps.stepSummary: The text returns to the rule that a person does not interrupt prayer even when a snake is wrapped around his heel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if a snake is wrapped around his heel, he does not interrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier rule about danger during prayer. This line sets up the qualification that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule names a snake specifically. רב ששת will use that detail to distinguish a different dangerous creature.

phrases.english: Even if a snake is wrapped around his heel,
he does not interrupt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the completed story back to the rule about interrupting prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A snake wrapped around a person’s heel does not, by itself, require interrupting prayer.

steps.title: A scorpion is treated differently
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת limits the no-interruption rule to a snake; with a scorpion, the person interrupts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: They taught this only about a snake. But for a scorpion, he interrupts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת narrows the rule just quoted. He says it does not give the same instruction for a scorpion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule remains in place for the snake case. רב ששת adds a different outcome for a scorpion: the person stops praying.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
They taught this only about a snake.
But for a scorpion, he interrupts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא נָחָשׁ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the preceding no-interruption rule to its stated snake case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One does not interrupt for the snake in the stated case, but does interrupt for a scorpion.

steps.title: A pit of snakes raises an objection
steps.stepSummary: A source permits testimony that someone who fell into a pit full of snakes and scorpions died, raising a difficulty for the distinction just made.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection is raised: If someone fell into a lions’ den, they do not testify that he died. If he fell into a pit full of snakes and scorpions, they do testify that he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a rule about testimony after someone falls among dangerous animals. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source treats a pit full of snakes and scorpions as deadly enough to support testimony of death. That makes the snake’s danger harder to dismiss when explaining why the person praying does not interrupt.

phrases.english: An objection is raised: If he fell into a lions’ den—
they do not testify that he died.
If he fell into a pit full
of snakes and scorpions—
they testify that he died!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction between a snake and a scorpion by citing a case in which snakes are treated as deadly.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת’s distinction between the snake case and the scorpion case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If snakes in the cited pit are treated as certain to cause death, why does the prayer rule say not to interrupt for a snake?
steps.confusionAlert: The cited pit contains both snakes and scorpions. The next step explains why the snakes there are dangerous: the person's fall presses on them. That does not apply to a single undisturbed snake wrapped around a heel.

steps.title: Why the snakes in the pit are different
steps.stepSummary: The pit does not show that an undisturbed snake will necessarily attack.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case is different: because of the pressure, they cause harm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 6. Falling into a pit puts pressure on the snakes, making that case different from a snake near someone who is praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source about the pit concerns snakes disturbed by the fall. It therefore does not undo רב ששת’s distinction between a snake and a scorpion during prayer.

phrases.english: That case is different, because the pressure causes them to harm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the circumstances of the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pit source seems to show that snakes are dangerous enough to require interrupting prayer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The snakes in the pit are dangerous because the person’s fall presses against them.

steps.title: Interrupt prayer when oxen approach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק states that someone who sees oxen interrupts prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: If one sees oxen, one interrupts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another animal-danger case. רבי יצחק says that seeing oxen is a reason to stop praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds oxen to the discussion of when danger calls for an interruption. The next step gives distances that help explain the danger.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: רָאָה שְׁוָורִים — פּוֹסֵק.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said: If one sees oxen, one interrupts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: רָאָה שְׁוָורִים — פּוֹסֵק.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from resolving the snake case to a ruling about oxen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees oxen interrupts prayer.

steps.title: The safe distance from an ox
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיה’s teaching gives distances for staying away from different oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הושעיה taught: One keeps fifty cubits from a שור תם, an ox without a record of goring, and stays beyond sight of a שור מועד, an ox known to gore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב הושעיה’s teaching to support taking the danger of oxen seriously. It gives a different distance for each kind of ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an ox without a record of goring requires distance. An ox known to gore requires still more distance, helping explain why רבי יצחק permits an interruption.

keyTerms.meaning: an ox without a record of goring
a cubit, a unit of length
as far as the eye can see

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָה: מַרְחִיקִין מִשּׁוֹר תָּם
phrases.english: As Rav Hoshaya taught: One keeps away from an ox without a record of goring

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה, וּמִשּׁוֹר מוּעָד — כִּמְלוֹא עֵינָיו.
phrases.english: fifty cubits, and from an ox known to gore—as far as the eye can see.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָה: מַרְחִיקִין מִשּׁוֹר תָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a teaching about oxen that supports רבי יצחק’s warning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הושעיה’s teaching about how far to stay from a שׁוֹר תָּם and a שׁוֹר מוּעָד.

steps.title: A strong warning to get away from an ox
steps.stepSummary: A teaching in the name of רבי מאיר urges someone to escape even while an ox is eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: While the ox’s head is in the basket, climb to the roof and throw away the ladder beneath you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a vivid warning about an ox. It says not to rely on the ox being busy eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The instruction to climb up and remove the ladder stresses how urgently one should get away. The next step specifies the kind of ox and time to which this warning applies.

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
While the ox’s head is in the basket—
climb onto the roof and throw away the ladder from beneath you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a vivid safety warning after the distances given by רב הושעיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Get away from the ox even when it appears occupied with food.

steps.title: When the strong warning applies
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the preceding warning to a black ox during ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: These words apply to a black ox during the days of ניסן, because the שטן dances between its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל narrows the warning just quoted. He says it applies to a black ox during ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “These words” points back to the warning about fleeing even while the ox eats. שמואל does not say that the earlier distances for other oxen no longer matter.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: These words apply
to a black ox during the days of Nisan,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַשָּׂטָן מְרַקֵּד לוֹ בֵּין קַרְנָיו.
phrases.english: because Satan dances between its horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the especially strong warning stated in רבי מאיר’s name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The preceding warning is specified for a black ox during ניסן.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן דוסא and the creature in the hole
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell how רבי חנינא בן דוסא confronted a harmful עַרְוָד, which bit him and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: In one place, an עַרְוָד was harming people. They told רבי חנינא בן דוסא. He asked to see its hole, placed his heel over the opening, and the עַרְוָד came out, bit him, and died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the ox discussion and begins a story about רבי חנינא בן דוסא. This part tells how he confronted the עַרְוָד and what happened when it bit him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people report a dangerous creature, and רבי חנינא בן דוסא deliberately places his heel at its hole. The creature dies after biting him. The next step gives the explanation for that outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: the harmful creature in this story

phrases.english: The Sages taught: There was an incident in one place

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה עַרְוָד, וְהָיָה מַזִּיק אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת.
phrases.english: where there was an arvad, and it was harming people.

phrases.aramaic: בָּאוּ וְהוֹדִיעוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא.
phrases.english: They came and informed Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: הַרְאוּ לִי אֶת חוֹרוֹ!
phrases.english: He said to them: Show me its hole!
They showed him its hole.
He placed his heel over the opening of the hole,
it came out and bit him—and that arvad died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ox warnings and opens a narrative involving a dangerous creature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This is an incident being reported, not a new general instruction to approach dangerous creatures.

steps.title: The dead creature becomes a lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא brings the dead עַרְוָד to the בית המדרש and tells his listeners to focus on sin, not the creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: He carried it on his shoulder to the בית המדרש and said: “See, my children: it is not the עַרְוָד that kills; rather, sin kills.”
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי חנינא בן דוסא shows the dead עַרְוָד to the people in the בית המדרש. He states the lesson he wants them to take from what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creature was dangerous, but רבי חנינא בן דוסא does not want the listeners to focus only on its bite. He directs their attention to חֵטְא as the deeper danger in this story.

keyTerms.meaning: the dangerous creature in the story

phrases.english: He placed it on his shoulder
and brought it to the study hall.
He said to them: See, my children,
it is not the arvad that kills,
rather, sin kills.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְטָלוֹ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וֶהֱבִיאוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the account of the harmful עַרְוָד from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא teaches that the lesson of this encounter concerns חֵטְא, not just the creature.

steps.title: The onlookers sum up the encounter
steps.stepSummary: The onlookers contrast the danger an עַרְוָד poses to a person with what happened when it met רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment they said: “Woe to a person who encounters an עַרְוָד, and woe to an עַרְוָד that encounters רבי חנינא בן דוסא.”
steps.whatsHappening: The onlookers close the story with a pointed saying. Its second half reverses the usual danger: this time the עַרְוָד was the one that died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half acknowledges that an עַרְוָד normally threatens a person. The second half highlights how unusual its encounter with רבי חנינא בן דוסא was.
steps.whatToRemember: The saying closes the עַרְוָד story; the next line starts a new משנה.

phrases.english: At that moment they said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁפָּגַע בּוֹ עַרְוָד,
phrases.english: Woe to the person who encountered an arvad,
and woe to the arvad

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁפָּגַע בּוֹ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא.
phrases.english: that encountered Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the onlookers’ closing reaction to רבי חנינא בן דוסא’s lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The onlookers describe the encounter as dangerous for an ordinary person but fatal for the עַרְוָד that met רבי חנינא בן דוסא.

steps.title: Where the two rain additions belong
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה places the mention of rain in תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים and the request for rain in בִּרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One mentions the might of the rains in the blessing about revival of the dead, and the request for rain in the blessing of the years.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and assigns two rain-related additions to two different blessings. It first states where rain is mentioned, then where rain is requested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning rain and asking for rain are separate parts of prayer here. The משנה puts each in a different blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessing concerning the year’s needs

phrases.english: Mishnah: One mentions the might of the rains
in the blessing about revival of the dead,
and the request for rain in the blessing of the years,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The עַרְוָד story has ended; the משנה opens a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rain mention belongs in תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, while the rain request belongs in בִּרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים.

steps.title: Where to say the distinction prayer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three positions for where הבדלה belongs within prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And הבדלה is in the blessing “Who grants knowledge.” רבי עקיבא says it is said as a separate fourth blessing. רבי אליעזר says it is in the blessing of thanksgiving.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to הבדלה and first gives its placement in חוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת. It then records different placements from רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three positions address where to say הבדלה within prayer. They differ about its location: inside חוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת, as its own fourth blessing, or in הוֹדָאָה.

keyTerms.meaning: the prayer distinguishing holy from ordinary
the blessing about God granting knowledge

phrases.english: And the distinction prayer is in “Who grants knowledge.”
Rabbi Akiva says:
One says it as a fourth blessing
on its own.
Rabbi Eliezer says: In thanksgiving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה’s list of prayer additions, now addressing הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה records three positions for the location of הבדלה in prayer.

steps.title: Why mention rain in that blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the rain rule and asks why that placement was chosen.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: “One mentions the might of the rains”—what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the first rain rule in the משנה and asks for its reason. This question sets up the next explanation; it does not yet provide one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already told us where to mention rain. The new question asks why that mention belongs specifically in the blessing about תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים.

phrases.english: Gemara: “One mentions the might of the rains”—
what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה’s הבדלה discussion, the גמרא returns to its earlier rain rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים mentioned in the blessing about תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים?

steps.title: Rain is as great as reviving the dead
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the mention of rain was placed in תחיית המתים because rain is equal in greatness to תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Because rain is equal to the reviving of the dead, they placed it in the blessing of reviving the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question from the last step: why do we mention rain in the blessing of תחיית המתים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer works by matching the topic to the blessing. Rain brings new life to the earth, so it is "weighed equal" to תחיית המתים. Because the two ideas match, the חכמים attached the mention of rain to that blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: They set it in place (the חכמים fixed it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the pattern for the whole section. Each insertion goes into the blessing whose theme it shares.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Because it [rain] is equal to the revival of the dead
phrases.notes: Rain brings new life to plants, like bringing the dead back to life.

phrases.english: therefore they placed it in the blessing of the revival of the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁשְּׁקוּלָה כִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the מאי טעמא of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rain matches תחיית המתים in greatness, so its mention belongs in that blessing.

steps.title: Why the request for rain goes in the blessing of the years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, that the request for rain is in ברכת השנים, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the request for rain is in the blessing of the years: what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second rule of the משנה and asks why the request for rain goes in ברכת השנים. This sets up רב יוסף's next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made a difference between mentioning rain (praise) and asking for rain (a request). Since the asking was put in a different blessing, the גמרא wants to know the reason for that placement too.

keyTerms.meaning: Request (here, the actual request for rain)
The blessing of the years, "ברך עלינו"

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הזכרה (mentioning rain, "משיב הרוח") with שאלה (asking for rain, "ותן טל ומטר"). They are two different insertions in two different blessings.

phrases.english: And the request [for rain] is in the blessing of the years:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה from Step 15.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as Step 17, now asked about the second rule of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the request for rain is placed in ברכת השנים.

steps.title: Rain is sustenance, so it goes in the blessing for sustenance
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that rain is פרנסה, so the request for it belongs in the blessing for פרנסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Because it is sustenance, they placed it in the blessing of sustenance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers why the request for rain is in ברכת השנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת השנים is our request for a good year and for food. Rain makes the crops grow, so it is part of our פרנסה. That is why the request for rain fits naturally inside the blessing that asks for פרנסה.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing for sustenance, which is ברכת השנים

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף gives the same kind of reason twice. Praising rain matches תחיית המתים, and asking for rain matches the request for פרנסה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Because it [rain] is sustenance,
therefore they placed it in the blessing of sustenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהִיא פַּרְנָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19, using the same pattern as Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rain is sustenance, so the request for it goes in the blessing for sustenance.

steps.title: Why הבדלה goes in the blessing of knowledge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that הבדלה is said in חונן הדעת and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: הבדלה is in "Who graciously grants knowledge": what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same "why" question about the third insertion, הבדלה in חונן הדעת. This sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of the opinions in the משנה about where הבדלה goes (Step 16). The גמרא wants the link between separating שבת from the weekdays and the blessing for knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: Separation; the prayer that separates שבת from the weekdays
"Who graciously grants knowledge", the fourth blessing of the עמידה
The night after שבת, when הבדלה is said in prayer

phrases.english: Havdala is in "Who graciously grants knowledge":
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה from Step 16.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of "why" questions, moving from rain to הבדלה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason הבדלה is inserted specifically in חונן הדעת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: הבדלה Needs Wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that הבדלה is placed in the blessing of wisdom because making a הבדלה is itself an act of wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Since הבדלה is a matter of wisdom, they placed it in the blessing of wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב יוסף's answer to the question from Step 21: why is הבדלה said in חונן הדעת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: To separate between holy and חול, you need understanding. To tell two things apart, you must first know how they differ. So the 'separating' prayer fits best in the blessing where we ask ה׳ for wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: They established it (set its place in the prayer)
The blessing of wisdom, i.e., אתה חונן

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Since it (havdalah) is wisdom,
phrases.notes: Telling things apart takes understanding.

phrases.english: they established it in the blessing of wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהִיא חָכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21, in the same style as רב יוסף's answers in Steps 18 and 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הבדלה requires wisdom, so it belongs in the blessing of wisdom.

steps.title: The רבנן: הבדלה Is About the Weekday
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן give a different reason: הבדלה is about חול, so it was placed in the first blessing said only on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: Since הבדלה is about חול, they placed it in a weekday blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the same question, from the רבנן. Their reason is different from רב יוסף's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three blessings of the עמידה are said on שבת too. חונן הדעת is the first blessing said only on weekdays. הבדלה marks the move from שבת into חול, so the רבנן place it right where the weekday part of the prayer begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A weekday blessing (one said only during the week)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree on the הלכה: הבדלה goes in חונן הדעת. They only disagree about the reason.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Since it (havdalah) is about the weekday,
phrases.notes: הבדלה brings us out of שבת and into the week.

phrases.english: therefore they established it in a weekday blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different reason for the same placement explained in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הבדלה is about חול, so it belongs in the first blessing said only on weekdays.

steps.title: Knowledge Is Great: It Opens the Weekday Blessings
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי praises דעה because it was placed as the very first of the weekday requests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said: Knowledge is great, because it was placed at the start of the weekday blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the blessing of wisdom just came up, the גמרא moves into a short side discussion praising דעה. This is the first statement in that discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the רבנן's point that חונן הדעת is the first weekday blessing. רב אמי sees that placement as a sign of importance. Before we ask for health, food, or anything else, we ask for understanding.

phrases.english: Rav Ami said:
Great is knowledge,
for it was placed at the beginning of the weekday blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion that grows out of the mention of the blessing of wisdom as the first weekday blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The placement of דעה first among the weekday blessings shows how important it is.

steps.title: Knowledge Sits Between Two Names of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי praises דעה again: in the פסוק 'כי אל דעות ה׳', the word for knowledge appears between two names of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי also said: Knowledge is great, because it was placed between two names of ה׳, as it says, 'For a God of knowledge is ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second praise of דעה from רב אמי, this time based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word 'דעות' sits between 'אל' and 'ה׳'. Being placed between two of ה׳'s names is treated as a sign of great importance.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'two letters'; here it means two names of ה׳
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two אותיות' does not mean two letters of the alphabet. It means two names of ה׳: אל and ה׳.

phrases.english: And Rav Ami said:
Great is knowledge,
for it was placed between two 'letters' (names of God),
as it is said: 'For God of knowledge is the Lord.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א ב:ג. דעות sits between אל and ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: גְּדוֹלָה דֵּעָה, שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second praise of דעה from the same speaker, now based on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דעה is great because a פסוק places it between two names of ה׳.

steps.title: No Mercy for One Without Knowledge
steps.stepSummary: Continuing his words, רב אמי says it is forbidden to have mercy on someone who has no דעה, and proves it from a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who has no knowledge, it is forbidden to have mercy on him, as it says: 'For they are not a people of understanding, therefore their Maker will not have mercy on them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי continues his praise of דעה with a strong statement about someone who lacks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because דעה is so important, lacking it is treated very seriously. The פסוק says ה׳ does not have mercy on a people without understanding. רב אמי learns from this that people also should not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to have mercy on him

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how highly the גמרא values דעה. Lacking it is not treated as a small flaw.

phrases.english: And anyone who has no knowledge —
it is forbidden to have mercy on him,
as it is said: 'For they are not a people of understanding,'
'therefore their Maker will not have mercy on them.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה כז:יא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אמי's statement. After praising דעה, he states what follows for someone who lacks it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who lacks דעה should not be shown mercy, as learned from ישעיה כז:יא.

steps.title: The מקדש Also Sits Between Two Names of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses the same idea to praise the מקדש, which a פסוק places between two names of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The מקדש is great, because it was placed between two names of ה׳, as it says: 'You made, ה׳, the מקדש, ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel praise from רבי אלעזר, using the same 'between two names' idea, now for the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק from אז ישיר, the word 'מקדש' sits between two mentions of ה׳. This matches רב אמי's teaching about דעה. Both are honored by being placed between two names of ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: הבדלה is said in חונן הדעת. רב יוסף says this is because it needs wisdom; the רבנן say it is because it is about חול. Both דעה and the מקדש are called 'great' because each appears between two names of ה׳ in a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Great is the Temple,
for it was placed between two 'letters' (names of God),
as it is said: 'You have made, Lord, the Temple, Lord.'
phrases.notes: שמות טו:יז. מקדש sits between two mentions of ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גָּדוֹל מִקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנִּתַּן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'between two names of ה׳' pattern from Step 25 to the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקדש is great because a פסוק places it between two names of ה׳.

steps.title: A person with knowledge is like one in whose days the Temple was built
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר connects the two praises: דעה and מקדש are each placed between two names of ה׳, so a person with דעה is like someone in whose days the בית המקדש was built.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any person who has knowledge, it is as if the בית המקדש was built in his days. Knowledge was placed between two names of ה׳, and the מקדש was placed between two names of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר takes the two ideas we just learned (דעה between two names of ה׳, and מקדש between two names of ה׳) and joins them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, the same pattern was used to praise דעה and to praise the מקדש. Since both share this special placement, רבי אלעזר says they are equal in importance. So having real understanding is as precious as having the בית המקדש built in your lifetime.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'two letters'; here it means two names of ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: "שתי אותיות" does not mean two letters of the alphabet. It refers to two names of ה׳ in the פסוק: "אל דעות ה׳" for דעה, and "פעלת ה׳ מקדש ה׳" for the מקדש.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any person who has knowledge
it is as if the Holy Temple was built in his days.
phrases.notes: He means it's worth that much, not that the Temple was really built in his days.

phrases.english: Knowledge was placed between two 'letters' (names of ה׳),
phrases.notes: "כי אל דעות ה׳" (שמואל א ב:ג)

phrases.english: the Temple was placed between two 'letters' (names of ה׳).
phrases.notes: "פעלת ה׳ מקדש ה׳" (שמות טו:יז)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 27's praise of the מקדש by linking it to the praise of דעה from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Having דעה is as valuable as having the בית המקדש built in one's days, because both are placed between two names of ה׳.

steps.title: Then revenge should also be great
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא קרחינאה attacks the method: if appearing between two names of ה׳ shows greatness, then נקמה (revenge) must also be great, since "אל נקמות ה׳" puts it between two names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא קרחינאה challenged this: If so, then revenge is great too, since it was placed between two names of ה׳, as it says: "God of vengeance, ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא קרחינאה challenges the whole method of proof. He shows that it seems to lead to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was: something placed between two names of ה׳ is great. But נקמה also appears that way in תהלים צד. Revenge is usually seen as a bad trait, so either the rule is wrong or we must say revenge is great.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (then this strange result follows)

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa Karḥina'a strongly objected to it:
But if so,
great is revenge
since it was placed between two 'letters' (names of ה׳),
as it is stated: "God of vengeance, ה׳"!
phrases.notes: תהלים צד:א

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא קַרְחִינָאָה אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'between two names of ה׳' method used in steps 25, 27, and 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that placement between two names of ה׳ shows greatness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule would make נקמה great, which seems wrong.

steps.title: Yes, revenge in its proper place is great
steps.stepSummary: The answer accepts the result: yes, when used in its proper setting, נקמה is great.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. At least in its proper place, it is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer does not reject the rule. It agrees that נקמה is great, but only in the right situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving up the rule, the answer accepts its result with a limit. Revenge is not always good, but when it is truly needed (like ה׳ punishing evil), it is a great thing. So the rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In its proper matter or setting

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
at least in its proper place, it is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29 by accepting its result with a limit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the result with a limit (בִּמִילְּתַהּ: in its proper context)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Revenge is always a bad trait, so the 'two names' rule must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Revenge in its proper setting really is great, so the rule holds.

steps.title: עולא's teaching on the two mentions of vengeance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer with עולא's teaching: the two mentions of נקמות in the פסוק stand for one vengeance for good and one for harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what עולא said: Why are these two 'vengeances' mentioned? One is for good and one is for harm. For good, as it is written: "He appeared from הר פארן." For harm, as it is written: "God of vengeance, ה׳; God of vengeance, appear."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings עולא's teaching to back up the idea that revenge can sometimes be a good and fitting thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "אל נקמות" twice, and עולא explains that each one has a different job. One is linked to "הופיע מהר פארן" (מתן תורה), so it is vengeance for good. The other is for harm. This shows that vengeance has a proper, positive place.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what was said), linking to a supporting teaching
Appeared, shone forth; the shared word linking the two פסוקים

phrases.english: And this is what Ulla said:
Why are these two 'vengeances' (mentioned)?
One is for good, and one is for harm.
For good, as it is written: "He appeared from Mount Paran."
phrases.notes: דברים לג:ב, about מתן תורה

phrases.english: For harm, as it is written:
"God of vengeance, ה׳; God of vengeance, appear."
phrases.notes: תהלים צד:א

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 30 with an earlier teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That נקמה can be great in its proper place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's reading of the double "אל נקמות", linked through the word "הופיע" to "הופיע מהר פארן".
steps.whatToRemember: Being placed between two names of ה׳ shows greatness: דעה, מקדש, and even נקמה when it is used in its proper place.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי עקיבא's view on הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי עקיבא: הבדלה is said as its own fourth ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: One says it as a fourth blessing, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about praising דעה is finished. The גמרא now returns to the משנה and quotes רבי עקיבא's opinion, setting up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained why the first opinion puts הבדלה inside the ברכה of חונן הדעת. Now it turns to רבי עקיבא, who says הבדלה gets its own separate fourth ברכה. This quote opens the next topic for analysis.

keyTerms.meaning: A fourth blessing; here, a separate ברכה for הבדלה
Etc., showing the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
One says it (הבדלה) as a fourth blessing, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר אוֹמְרָהּ בְּרָכָה רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about דעה and returns to the משנה's dispute about הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, הבדלה is said as an independent fourth ברכה in the תפלה of מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: Why don't we know where הבדלה was placed?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא asks רבי יוחנן why we cannot simply look up where אנשי כנסת הגדולה placed הבדלה in the תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: Since אנשי כנסת הגדולה set up for ישראל all the blessings, prayers, קידוש and הבדלה, let's just see where they set it up.
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks his teacher a basic question about the argument in the משנה over where הבדלה goes. This question sets up רבי יוחנן's historical answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had several opinions about where הבדלה goes, such as its own ברכה or inside חונן הדעת. רב שמן's point is that one authoritative body wrote all these texts, so the original placement should be known. Why is there any argument at all?

keyTerms.meaning: The Men of the Great Assembly, the sages of early בית שני who set up the prayers
Now, since (introduces a known fact as the basis for a question)
הבדלה blessings, which separate holy time from ordinary time

steps.confusionAlert: רב שמן is not asking whether הבדלה exists or who made it up. He is asking why its exact place in the תפלה is unclear.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Now, since the Men of the Great Assembly
instituted for Israel
blessings and prayers, sanctifications and havdalahs,
phrases.notes: The same group set up all of these texts.

phrases.english: let us see where they instituted it.
phrases.notes: Meaning: where in the עמידה they placed הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִכְּדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the משנה's dispute about where הבדלה goes, which was just revisited through רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the original placement of הבדלה in the תפלה is not known, given that one authoritative body set it up.

steps.title: הבדלה moved back and forth between תפלה and the כוס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that הבדלה kept changing location depending on the people's wealth. He adds that one who says it in תפלה must also say it over a כוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: At first they put it in the תפלה. When the people became rich, they put it on the cup of wine. When they became poor again, they went back and put it in the תפלה. And they said: One who says הבדלה in the תפלה must also say הבדלה over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the placement is unclear because הבדלה kept moving. Over time, people were no longer sure of its original spot in the תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In poor times, few people had wine, so הבדלה went into the תפלה. In rich times, it moved to the כוס, and in poor times it came back. Because of all these shifts, the exact spot in the עמידה was forgotten, which explains the argument in the משנה. The final rule is that saying it in תפלה does not remove the need to say it over a כוס.

keyTerms.meaning: They established it, meaning they fixed its place
Cup of wine used for הבדלה
One who says הבדלה in the עמידה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for our practice today: we say אתה חוננתנו in the עמידה and also make הבדלה over wine.

phrases.english: He said to him:
At first, they established it in the prayer.
phrases.notes: This was in the early, poor years of בית שני.

phrases.english: They became wealthy — they established it over the cup.
They became poor — they went back and established it in the prayer.
And they said: one who says havdalah in the prayer
must say havdalah over the cup.
phrases.notes: Commentators explain: if he is able to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שמן's question directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The placement became unclear because הבדלה shifted between תפלה and כוס as the people's wealth changed. Also, one who says it in תפלה must still say it over a כוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המבדיל בתפלה צריך שיבדיל על הכוס

steps.title: A second report of רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports the same teaching of רבי יוחנן word for word. This confirms the history and the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: אנשי כנסת הגדולה set up for ישראל blessings, prayers, קידוש and הבדלה. At first they put it in the תפלה. When the people became rich, they put it on the cup. When they became poor again, they put it in the תפלה. And they said: One who says הבדלה in the תפלה must also say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a separate chain of students who heard the same lesson from רבי יוחנן. The repetition shows the teaching was reliably passed down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words almost exactly match the previous step, but they come through a different student, רבי חייא בר אבא. This independent report supports the history and the הלכה that one says הבדלה in תפלה and also over a כוס.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces a parallel report)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. It is the same teaching of רבי יוחנן, repeated to show it was reliably passed down.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה תִּקְּנוּ לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: The Men of the Great Assembly instituted for Israel
blessings and prayers, sanctifications and havdalahs.
At first, they established it in the prayer.
They became wealthy — they established it over the cup.
They became poor again — they established it in the prayer.
And they said: one who says havdalah in the prayer
must say havdalah over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats רבי יוחנן's answer through a second student, as confirmation.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's history of הבדלה and the rule that one who says it in תפלה must also say it over a כוס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An independent report by רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף give the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both state that one who says הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבה and רב יוסף both said: One who says הבדלה in the תפלה must also say הבדלה over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more אמוראים who hold the same הלכה. They state only the bottom-line rule, without the history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the support comes from other teachers, not only from רבי יוחנן's students. It focuses only on the practical rule: saying הבדלה in תפלה is not enough, and one still needs a כוס.
steps.whatToRemember: הבדלה moved between תפלה and כוס as the people's wealth changed, which is why its exact spot in the עמידה became unclear. The halacha, reported by several sources, is that one who says הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who both said:
One who says havdalah in the prayer
must say havdalah over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further support for the rule's final line, from different אמוראים.
steps.raayaObject: The rule המבדיל בתפלה צריך שיבדיל על הכוס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The joint statement of רבה and רב יוסף.

steps.title: רבא challenges the rule from a teaching about forgetting הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא saying that one who forgot הבדלה in חונן הדעת does not repeat the תפלה, because he 'can' say it over a כוס. This suggests the כוס is optional, not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We have a problem with our rule. A teaching says: if someone mistakenly left out the mention of rain in the blessing about bringing the dead back to life, or left out the request for rain in the blessing of the years, he must go back and repeat. But if he left out הבדלה in 'Who grants knowledge,' he does not go back, because he is able to say it over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the rule from the last few steps, that one who says הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס. He uses a ברייתא whose wording seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'because he CAN say it over the כוס.' That wording sounds like the כוס is an optional backup, used only if one forgot it in תפלה. If so, someone who already said הבדלה in תפלה would not need the כוס at all, which contradicts רבי יוחנן, רבה, and רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: And we raise an objection against our own teaching
The mention of God's power of rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם)
The request for rain (ותן טל ומטר)
The blessing of the years (ברך עלינו), asking for a good harvest
We make him go back and repeat

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the rule is wrong. He is pointing out a wording problem that seems to clash with it. The next step fixes the wording.

phrases.english: Rava said, and we raise an objection to our teaching:
If one erred and did not mention
the might of rain in the blessing of the revival of the dead
or the request for rain in the blessing of the years
we make him go back,
but if he left out havdala in 'Who grants knowledge'
we do not make him go back,
because he is able to say it over the cup.
phrases.notes: The word 'able' (יכול) is the source of the difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated by רבה and רב יוסף (and רבי יוחנן) that הבדלה in תפלה still requires a כוס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one who says הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's phrase 'because he CAN say it over the כוס' implies the כוס is only an optional substitute, so it is not an independent obligation.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: 'he says it' instead of 'he can say it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the reading of the ברייתא from 'because he can say it over the כוס' to 'because he says it over the כוס.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'because he is able to say it over the cup.' Rather, say 'because he says it over the cup.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's challenge by changing one word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, the ברייתא no longer calls the כוס optional. It says he does not repeat the תפלה because he will say הבדלה over the כוס anyway, as is required. So the כוס is a regular obligation, which fits the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say (do not read it this way)
That he says it (a fixed practice, not just a possibility)

phrases.english: Do not say:
'because he is able to say it over the cup,'
rather say:
'because he says it over the cup.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by changing the wording of the ברייתא he quoted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא reads 'can say it,' making the כוס optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reads 'says it,' meaning the כוס is a standard requirement, so the rule stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן directly rules that the כוס is still required
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנימין בר יפת reports that רבי יוחנן was asked whether one who said הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס, and he answered yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי בנימין בר יפת said: רבי יוסי asked רבי יוחנן in ציידן (some say it was רבי שמעון בן יעקב from צור who asked רבי יוחנן), and I heard it: 'One who says הבדלה in prayer, must he also say it over the cup, or not?' And he answered: 'He must say it over the cup.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more support for the rule. It quotes an eyewitness report of רבי יוחנן ruling on exactly this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a deduction from wording. It is a clear question and a clear answer from רבי יוחנן. It backs up the corrected reading of the ברייתא and confirms that saying הבדלה in תפלה does not remove the need for a כוס.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces supporting testimony)

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule of this part: even someone who said הבדלה in תפלה must still say it over a כוס.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֶת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּצַיְדָּן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei asked Rabbi Yochanan in Sidon,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Shimon ben Yaakov
from Tyre who asked Rabbi Yochanan,
and I heard it:
One who recites havdala in the prayer,

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּבְדִּיל עַל הַכּוֹס, אוֹ לֹא?
phrases.english: must he recite havdala over the cup, or not?
And he said to him:
He must recite havdala over the cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the corrected reading from step 38 with direct testimony of רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who says הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Testimony of רבי בנימין בר יפת, who heard רבי יוחנן answer the question directly.

steps.title: The reverse question: after הבדלה over a cup, is it still said in תפלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the opposite question: if someone already said הבדלה over a כוס, must he still say it in תפלה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: one who already said הבדלה over the cup, what is the law about saying it in prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the first direction is settled, the גמרא opens a new question in the opposite direction. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know that הבדלה in תפלה does not exempt the כוס. The open question is whether the כוס exempts תפלה. This could happen, for example, if someone made הבדלה over wine before davening מעריב. The answer comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. The rule already decided is תפלה first, then the כוס is still required. This new question is the reverse: the כוס first, then is תפלה still required?

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
One who recited havdala over the cup,
what is the law regarding reciting havdala in the prayer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling that הבדלה in תפלה still requires a כוס, the גמרא asks the reverse case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether saying הבדלה over a כוס exempts one from saying it in תפלה.

steps.title: A logical argument: הבדלה over a כוס does not exempt you from saying it in תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק uses a קל וחומר to show that someone who said הבדלה over a כוס must still say it in תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We can learn this with a קל וחומר from תפלה. תפלה is the main place where הבדלה was established, and yet the rule is that someone who said הבדלה in תפלה must also say it over a כוס. So someone who said הבדלה over a כוס, which is not the main place it was established, must certainly also say it in תפלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 40. Yes, someone who said הבדלה over a כוס must still say it in תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument compares the 'stronger' form of הבדלה with the 'weaker' one. הבדלה in תפלה is the original, main enactment, and even it is not enough by itself. So the כוס, which was added later and is less central, certainly cannot be enough by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (or the reverse): 'if this is true here, it is surely true there'
The main, original enactment of the חכמים
All the more so (it must be true)

steps.whyThisMatters: Together with steps 36–39, this sets up the view that each form of הבדלה is required on its own: תפלה does not exempt the כוס, and the כוס does not exempt תפלה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It follows a fortiori from prayer.
Just as prayer,
which is the main enactment,
they said: one who recites havdala in prayer
must recite havdala over the cup.
One who recites havdala over the cup,
which is not the main enactment,
all the more so (must he also say it in prayer)!
phrases.notes: The 'all the more so' means he must certainly also say הבדלה in תפלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 40.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one who said הבדלה over a כוס must still say it in תפלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. By a קל וחומר from the rule that תפלה (the main enactment) does not exempt the כוס, the כוס (not the main enactment) surely does not exempt תפלה.

steps.title: A ברייתא praising הבדלה in תפלה and blessing one who does both
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא אריכא teaches a ברייתא: הבדלה in תפלה is more praiseworthy than over a כוס, and one who does both deserves blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the tall taught a ברייתא before רב חיננא: Someone who says הבדלה in תפלה is more praiseworthy than someone who says it over a כוס. And if he said הבדלה in both, may blessings rest on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא is brought into the discussion. It ranks הבדלה in תפלה above הבדלה over a כוס and praises doing both. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will find a problem inside this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line suggests that each form works alone, with תפלה simply being the better one. The second line praises doing both. These two ideas will clash in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: May blessings rest on his head

phrases.english: Rav Acha the tall taught
before Rav Chinnana:
One who recites havdala in prayer is more praiseworthy
than one who recites havdala over the cup.
And if he recited havdala in this and in that,
may blessings rest upon his head.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב אַחָא אֲרִיכָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new ברייתא on the same topic, which seems to treat one form of הבדלה as enough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הבדלה in תפלה is preferable to over a כוס, and one who says it in both is blessed.

steps.title: The ברייתא contradicts itself: doing both would be an unnecessary ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא contradicts itself. If תפלה alone is enough, then saying הבדלה again over a כוס is a ברכה שאינה צריכה, which violates 'לא תשא'. So how can such a person be praised?
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult! You said that one who says הבדלה in תפלה is more praiseworthy than one who says it over a כוס, which shows that תפלה alone is enough. Then you taught that if he said it in both, may blessings rest on his head. But once he fulfilled his obligation with one, he is exempt, and the second is a ברכה שאינה צריכה. And רב (some say ריש לקיש, and others say both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש) said: Anyone who says an unnecessary ברכה transgresses 'לא תשא'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the inside. Its first half and second half do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half implies that one הבדלה fulfills the obligation. If so, a second הבדלה is extra and unnecessary, and an unnecessary ברכה is a serious problem, since it takes ה׳'s name in vain. So the second half cannot be praising someone for doing both.

keyTerms.meaning: This (text) itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)
'Do not take (ה׳'s name in vain)', the prohibition of saying ה׳'s name for no purpose

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not about which form of הבדלה is better. It is about whether doing both is praiseworthy or forbidden. If one is enough, the second ברכה is a violation, not a merit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step brings in the important general rule that a ברכה שאינה צריכה is forbidden under 'לא תשא'.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: one who recites havdala in prayer is more praiseworthy
than one who recites havdala over the cup,
evidently prayer alone is sufficient.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי אִם הִבְדִּיל בְּזוֹ וּבָזוֹ —
phrases.english: And then it teaches: if he recited havdala in this and in that,
may blessings rest upon his head.
But since he fulfilled his obligation with one, he is exempt,
and it becomes an unnecessary blessing,
and Rav said, and some say Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
who both said:
Anyone who recites an unnecessary blessing
transgresses 'Do not take (the Name in vain)'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא brought in step 42.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second clause of רב אחא's ברייתא: 'if he recited havdala in both, may blessings rest upon his head'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause implies one הבדלה suffices. So a second הבדלה is a ברכה שאינה צריכה, which violates 'לא תשא' and cannot be praiseworthy.

steps.title: Fixing the ברייתא: blessings come to one who says it in one and not the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of the ברייתא: the blessing is for one who said הבדלה in one place and did not repeat it in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: If he said הבדלה in this one and did not say it in that one, may blessings rest on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by changing the text of the ברייתא's second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, the praise goes to someone who did הבדלה once and did not add an unnecessary second ברכה. Now both halves of the ברייתא agree that one הבדלה is enough, and the problem of 'לא תשא' disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Say it like this (an emendation of the text)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the corrected ברייתא, one הבדלה is enough, and repeating it would be a ברכה שאינה צריכה. This view sits in tension with the earlier opinions (רבה, רב יוסף, רבי יוחנן, רב נחמן בר יצחק) that require both.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this ברייתא with steps 36–41. Those opinions say both forms of הבדלה are required. This ברייתא, as corrected, says one is enough. They are different views.

phrases.english: Rather, say as follows:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הִבְדִּיל בְּזוֹ וְלֹא הִבְדִּיל בָּזוֹ —
phrases.english: If he recited havdala in this and did not recite havdala in that,
may blessings rest upon his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the internal contradiction raised in step 43 by emending the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא praises one who says הבדלה in both תפלה and over a כוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא praises one who says הבדלה in one and does not repeat it in the other, avoiding a ברכה שאינה צריכה.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks about someone who erred in both places
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב ששת what the law is if someone made a mistake in הבדלה both in תפלה and over the כוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked רב ששת: If someone made a mistake in this one and in that one, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks a new question. What happens if a person messed up הבדלה both in the תפלה and over the כוס?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the גמרא dealt with someone who said הבדלה in one place and asked whether he must also say it in the other. Now the case is worse: he did not succeed in either place. רב חסדא wants to know what such a person must do.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher or colleague)
He made a mistake / he erred (here, forgot הבדלה)
In this one and in that one (in תפלה and over the כוס)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda asked Rav Sheshet:
phrases.notes: This is the usual way of asking a question about הלכה.

phrases.english: If one erred in this and in that, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "This and that" means הבדלה in תפלה and הבדלה over the כוס.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the wording of the ברייתא about one who said הבדלה in one place, the גמרא asks about someone who failed in both places.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What must a person do if he forgot or erred in הבדלה both in תפלה and over the כוס?

steps.title: רב ששת rules that he goes back to the beginning
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that one who erred in both places must go back to the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: One who made a mistake in this one and in that one goes back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רב חסדא's question. A person who erred in both places goes back to the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the person did not fulfill הבדלה anywhere, he cannot rely on either one. So he must start over: he repeats the תפלה (the עמידה) and also says הבדלה over the כוס.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes back to the beginning (starts over)

steps.whatToRemember: If someone made a mistake in הבדלה both in תפלה and over the כוס, he has not fulfilled הבדלה at all, so he must go back to the beginning.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with the earlier cases. Earlier, the person said הבדלה correctly in one place. Here he failed in both places, and that is why he must start over.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב ששת answering רב חסדא.

phrases.english: One who erred in this and in that
phrases.notes: Repeating the case from the question.

phrases.english: returns to the beginning.
phrases.notes: He starts over, repeating both the תפלה and the הבדלה over the כוס.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טָעָה בְּזוֹ וּבָזוֹ — חוֹזֵר לָרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב חסדא's question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who erred in both תפלה and כוס goes back to the beginning and repeats both.
